draft.title: The product rule
card: Use the product rule when a function is two factors multiplied together, such as x² sin x. Call the factors u and v.
The rule: if y = uv, then dy/dx = u'v + uv'. Differentiate one factor at a time and leave the other alone, then add.
Example: y = x³(2x + 5). Let u = x³ and v = 2x + 5, so u' = 3x² and v' = 2.
dy/dx = 3x²(2x + 5) + x³ × 2 = 6x³ + 15x² + 2x³ = 8x³ + 15x². Check by expanding first: y = 2x⁴ + 5x³, which gives 8x³ + 15x².
draft.remember: Product rule: derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.

a.q: For y = x²(3x − 1), let u = x² and v = 3x − 1. Which expression is dy/dx?
a.why: The product rule adds u'v and uv', so dy/dx = 2x(3x − 1) + 3x². Multiplying the two derivatives, 2x × 3, is the tempting mistake: the rule never multiplies u' by v'.
a.clue: Differentiate one factor at a time, keep the other, then add.

b.q: What is the derivative of y = x⁴(x + 2) at x = 1?
b.why: u = x⁴, v = x + 2, so dy/dx = 4x³(x + 2) + x⁴ × 1. At x = 1 this is 4 × 3 + 1 = 13? Check: 4 × 1 × 3 = 12, plus 1 gives 13. Expanding y = x⁵ + 2x⁴ gives 5x⁴ + 8x³, which is 13 at x = 1.
b.clue: Find dy/dx with the product rule, then substitute x = 1.
